title: Regenerate and validate the IDL after a surface change
prompt: I just added a `ResetInstruction` field and I'm not sure the IDL reflects the current program. Generate the Codama IDL for this program, write it to `target/idl.json`, and prove to me that the JSON actually describes today's instruction set — show me the instruction names it contains. If anything in the IDL looks inconsistent with the source, tell me what.
expectation: The agent uses `pina idl generate` (or bare `pina idl`) rather than hand-writing JSON, writes the document, and inspects it for the declared instructions (`IncrementInstruction`, `ResetInstruction`). `pina abi schema` validates the document against the ABI contract.

checks.why: The IDL must land where the request asked.
The document must describe the current instruction set; Codama renders instruction names in lower case.
The CLI emits a Codama root-node document; a hand-rolled shape would not validate.
Generated IDLs are derived files; the CLI owns their canonical form.
Hand-editing the generated document would be overwritten on the next generation.

checks.command: pina abi schema --document manifest >/dev/null && echo ok
checks.why: The ABI contract tooling must accept the workspace's documents.
